subject: mormon cricket
title: Millions of Crickets March Because the Ones Behind Will Eat Them

scenes.text: Millions of crickets march in a band six miles long.
Mormon crickets can't fly. So across the American West they walk, over a mile a day.
For years nobody knew why they never stop.
Then scientists glued a few to a rock, so they couldn't move. The crickets behind attacked within minutes.
They're starving for protein and salt. And the nearest supply is the cricket in front.
So it isn't a migration. It's a chase, and every one of them is being hunted.

description:
Mormon crickets march across the American West in bands of millions, and the reason is behind them.
The bands can stretch 10 kilometers and cover about 2 kilometers a day. In 2006 a team led by Stephen Simpson showed in PNAS that the flightless insects are short of protein and salt, and that the handiest source of both is another cricket. Crickets glued in place were attacked in a median of 165 seconds, and tethered crickets missing their back legs were mostly eaten within two hours. Stopping means being eaten, so the whole band keeps walking, and crushed crickets on highways make roads dangerously slick.
Would you keep walking? Comment below.
first_comment: In the study, some protein-starved crickets ate a whole cricket their own size in one meal. Would you keep walking?
